articles.summary: Los analistas deportivos de 1xBet España han seleccionado a los mejores jugadores de la Segunda División española que tienen potencial para dar el salto a la máxima categoría en un futuro próximo
articles.body: La Segunda División cuenta con un gran listado de talentos, capaces de jugar en los mejores equipos de LaLiga. Estos son algunas de las joyas que se encuentran en la categoría de plata de nuestro país. Todo ello ha sido analiza por la casa de apuestas de 1XBET, donde podrás encontrar una gran variedad de cuotas para tus apuestas deportivas. Vladyslav Vanat, Girona Antes de trasladarse a España, Vanat fue el máximo goleador de la Premier League ucraniana durante dos años consecutivos, y en su primera temporada en España marcó 10 goles con el Girona: 9 en La Liga y 1 en la Copa del Rey. Es más, si este jugador no se hubiera lesionado justo antes de la recta final de la temporada 2025-26, su equipo habría conservado, casi con toda seguridad, su puesto en la primera división. Tras el descenso del club catalán a segunda división, el delantero ucraniano se quedó en el Girona y ya ha marcado un gol y ha dado una asistencia esta temporada. Si Vanat mantiene el mismo nivel de rendimiento, muy pronto podría tener una nueva oportunidad de demostrar su valía en La Liga. Sergio Arribas, Almería Al igual que Vanat, Arribas llegó a marcar una vez 9 goles en una temporada de La Liga. Tras el descenso del Almería, se quedó en el equipo y, en la segunda temporada del club en Segunda División, marcó 25 goles, convirtiéndose en el máximo goleador de la liga. Lo que resulta especialmente impresionante es que Sergio lograra estas estadísticas jugando principalmente como centrocampista ofensivo y no como delantero centro. Yáser Asprilla, Girona Hace dos años, el Girona fichó al colombiano por €18 millones, sin contar las primas, una cifra superior a la que jamás había pagado por ningún fichaje en toda su historia. Asprilla no estuvo a la altura de esa inversión al instante, pero ha tenido un comienzo muy productivo en la presente temporada: solo le han hecho falta 276 minutos sobre el terreno de juego para marcar 4 goles. Ousmane Camara, Castellón No hace mucho, Camara jugaba en el equipo juvenil del Auxerre, luego fue cedido al Annecy y ahora se ha consolidado en el Castellón. El delantero guineano ha comenzado la nueva temporada con cuatro goles y una asistencia en los seis primeros partidos, y figura entre los máximos goleadores de la Segunda División. Al mismo tiempo, Camara no se limita a jugar en el área de penalti: se desplaza hacia las bandas, a menudo se retrasa para recibir el balón y participa activamente en la construcción de las jugadas de ataque. Taisei Miyashiro, Las Palmas Antes de llegar a España, Miyashiro había disputado más de 160 partidos en la máxima categoría del fútbol japonés y también había debutado con su selección. En invierno, el jugador japonés se trasladó a las Islas Canarias, donde marcó 4 goles en 17 partidos de liga. Posteriormente, Las Palmas decidió ficharlo de forma definitiva procedente del Vissel Kobe y le ofreció un contrato vigente hasta 2030. Miyashiro ha comenzado la nueva temporada con la misma confianza, sumando 2 goles y 2 asistencias en los seis primeros partidos. Pablo Sáenz, Oviedo Sáenz tuvo su primera experiencia en La Liga en la primavera de 2024, cuando debutó con el Granada. La temporada pasada, mientras jugaba en segunda, el extremo marcó 4 goles y dio 2 asistencias antes de fichar por el Oviedo en verano. Pablo tuvo un buen comienzo con su nuevo equipo, a finales de agosto, la afición del Oviedo lo eligió como su Jugador del Mes. Brian Cipenga, Almería En verano, Cipenga se trasladó de Castellón a Almería y comenzó la nueva temporada con un gol y tres asistencias en sus primeros seis partidos. Este rendimiento no es nada nuevo para él, en febrero de la temporada pasada, el jugador congoleño también logró un gol y tres asistencias en cuatro partidos y fue nombrado Jugador del Mes de la Segunda División. La gran pregunta ahora es si Brian podrá mantener este nivel de rendimiento durante un periodo más largo. Gorka Gorosabel, Real Sociedad B Gorosabel solo tiene 20 años, pero en las siete primeras jornadas de la Segunda División, este centrocampista ya ha marcado dos goles y ha dado una asistencia. Si sigue rindiendo a este nivel con la Real Sociedad B, que según el reglamento, no puede ascender a La Liga, su siguiente paso podría ser dar el salto al primer equipo del club. Jon Guruzeta, Eibar La familia de Guruzeta no es ninguna desconocida en el fútbol español, su padre, Xabier, jugó en la Real Sociedad y en el Alavés, mientras que su hermano mayor, Gorka, juega actualmente en el Athletic de Bilbao. Ahora Jon también está dejando huella, suma 3 goles y 2 asistencias en sus primeros 7 partidos de la temporada. Pero la productividad de Guruzeta no es su único punto fuerte. Jon puede jugar en ambas bandas y detrás del delantero, lo que le convierte en un jugador especialmente valioso para el ataque del Eibar. Álex Forés, Burgos A diferencia de muchos de los jugadores que figuran en esta lista elaborada por 1xBet es, Forés ya ha pasado de la Segunda División a La Liga y viceversa. En la temporada 2023-24, Álex marcó 16 goles con el Villarreal B y, un año después, cedido en el Levante, ayudó al equipo a conseguir el ascenso. Sin embargo, el delantero pasó su temporada en La Liga con el Oviedo, donde también había sido cedido. En verano, Forés fichó por el Burgos y volvió a la Segunda División, donde comenzó la nueva campaña con 3 goles y 1 asistencia en 7 partidos. ¡Sigue los partidos de la Segunda División y apoya a tus favoritos con 1xBet!

articles.title: Daniel Dubois fears Fabio Wardley is “gambling with his life” ahead of brutal WBO heavyweight title rematch
articles.summary: Daniel Dubois has expressed serious concerns about Fabio Wardley’s health ahead of their highly anticipated heavyweight rematch.
articles.body: Daniel Dubois has expressed serious concerns about Fabio Wardley’s health ahead of their highly anticipated heavyweight rematch. The British boxer believes his rival is taking a major risk by stepping into the ring again after their brutal first encounter in May. Dubois stopped Wardley in the 11th round after surviving two knockdowns in a thrilling contest in Manchester.The rematch will see Dubois defend his WBO heavyweight title against Wardley, who is determined to reclaim the championship. However, Dubois believes the physical cost of boxing is a serious concern and fears another punishing fight could have lasting consequences for his opponent.Daniel Dubois warns Fabio Wardley about the risks of their rematchSpeaking on In Camp With, Daniel Dubois explained that he understands why Fabio Wardley accepted the rematch despite the punishment he suffered in their previous meeting.“He has no choice. He probably thinks he has nowhere else to go. It’s a world title fight and he wants to make money- like us all. He was never going to turn it down. He’s going to take another gamble. Fabio is gambling with his health, his life, like we all do. We are prize fighters. This is a sport, but it’s a blood sport”, he said per The Sun.Dubois’ comments reflect the dangers both men face as they prepare to fight again. The two heavyweights have developed powerful reputations, but their first meeting showed how quickly a fight can become dangerous.Wardley made a stunning start in their May contest. He landed a trademark looping right hand just nine seconds into the fight, catching Dubois around the temple. Another powerful right hand in the third round sent the champion to the canvas again.However, Dubois recovered and gradually took control of the contest. His trainer, Don Charles, reportedly gave him a slap around the chops before the fifth round to help him regain his focus.The fight then turned increasingly difficult for Wardley. Dubois landed repeated heavy punches, leaving his opponent with a badly damaged right eye and a bloodied, injured nose. The referee eventually stopped the contest in the 11th round.Dubois believes the damage sustained in such contests can have lasting effects on fighters. He explained that every fight takes something away from a boxer, regardless of the result.“Every fight changes you. Every fight takes a bit out of you. Every time you get in that ring, it takes a little bit out of you. I have to build up this amount of energy and intensity so that I’m just a monster in there. Boxing is a unique sport - it’s not even really a sport”, he said.Despite his concerns, Dubois understands that he must approach the rematch as a professional. He also made it clear that he cannot hold back if Wardley and his team are prepared to continue.The rivals first met in 2017, when they sparred at the Peacock Gym in Canning Town. articles.title: Renee Montgomery Defends Dual Role As WNBA Analyst and Dream Owner
articles.summary: Montgomery played 11 years in the WNBA, including two with Atlanta.
articles.body:
SAN FRANCISCO — Renee Montgomery has several roles to juggle. She is a studio analyst for USA Network's WNBA coverage, manages a production company, leads her own foundation, and is launching a new podcast, Checkmate , in November.

She's also the co-owner of the Atlanta Dream, one of the franchises competing in the WNBA Finals—which she will be covering. USA Network will air the WNBA Finals for the first time, broadcasting Games 2, 3, 5, and 6.

Given she has a stake in one of the two Finals teams, people could assume she is biased. She's often at Dream home games and was on the sidelines celebrating with the players when they clinched a spot in the Finals last week. (USA Network did not air any of the semifinal series.)

But Montgomery, who played 11 years in the WNBA, says she leverages her experience as a player to analyze games without bias.

"I love the sport so much that you have to cover it a certain way," Montgomery told Front Office Sports . "Like I understand the effort, I understand the grind, I understand all the sacrifice that went into a player having a good game. So whether or not that player is playing for the Atlanta Dream doesn't matter. I have to analyze the game for what I see."

She told FOS there aren't any rules imposed on her by USA Network or her other employers. A source with USA Network confirmed to FOS that she has no restrictions.

"I'm sure that if I had companies that I worked for that felt like there was a bias, I'm sure that they would let me know," Montgomery said.

She said it might be different if she was calling games because play-by-play commentators and game analysts are generally present at each game and can therefore talk to players and coaches at shootaround or pregame.

In the NFL, Tom Brady , a game analyst for FOX, is a part-owner of the Raiders. The NFL restricts him from entering practice facilities or attending other teams' practices, though he is allowed to call Las Vegas games.

articles.title: El Balón de Oro vuelve a dar un vuelco
articles.standfirst: Betfair coloca a Kane como favorito, de nuevo
articles.summary: Betfair coloca a Kane como favorito, de nuevo
articles.body: Las votaciones están cerradas desde el 28 de septiembre, el recuento es secreto y la gala no llegará hasta el 26 de octubre, pero el mercado no ha parado de moverse en las casas de apuestas. En las últimas semanas, el Balón de Oro ha pasado por tres fases bien distintas, y la última ha devuelto a Harry Kane al primer puesto en las apuestas, con Lamine Yamal como único rival real. La historia empezó con un claro dominio inglés. A principios de septiembre, Kane aparecía como favorito casi indiscutible. En los mercados de predicción, las opciones del delantero del Bayern rondaban el 64 %, frente a un 15 % de Yamal. En las casas de apuestas, las cuotas citadas por los medios españoles llegaron a situarlo en 1.65, con el azulgrana a 3.75. Se trataba de un delantero de 33 años con 73 goles entre club y selección, un triplete doméstico en Alemania y la candidatura más sólida en cifras. Después llegó el giro. Poco antes del cierre del plazo, Yamal empezó a escalar. Los argumentos de su candidatura también tenían peso: campeón de LaLiga y campeón del Mundo con España. La tercera fase es la actual. Con todo apuntando a que el barcelonista había asaltado el liderato, las casas de apuestas han vuelto a colocar a Kane en cabeza. Betfair paga ahora el triunfo del inglés a 1.62 (una probabilidad implícita del 62 %) y el de Yamal a 2.00 (50 %). Más abajo, Kylian Mbappé se paga a 13 (7,7 %) y Leo Messi a 17 (5,9 %). El mercado ha dejado la carrera en un cara a cara. Conviene hacer una puntualización importante. Las votaciones están cerradas, así que ningún movimiento posterior puede cambiar el resultado. Un giro de cuotas, a estas alturas, no refleja votos, sino precio: dinero apostado, liquidez, exposición de las casas y, sobre todo, rumores. En años anteriores, los favoritos del mercado en esta fase no siempre han acabado ganando, y la propia organización ha insistido en que el recuento no se conocerá hasta la ceremonia. El contexto también juega a favor del inglés en algunos aspectos. La gala se celebrará por primera vez en Londres, en el London Palladium, la ciudad natal de Kane, un detalle simbólico que no vota pero influye en el relato. En el otro lado, Yamal llega con una narrativa casi irresistible. Sería el jugador más joven en ganar el trofeo, tras quedar segundo el año pasado, cuando Kane acabó decimotercero en la votación oficial. El jurado está formado por cien periodistas, uno por cada uno de los cien mejores países del ranking FIFA, y el periodo evaluado va del 3 de agosto de 2025 al 19 de julio de 2026, incluido el Mundial. Ese criterio suele penalizar a los jugadores cuya mejor imagen llega en los meses previos al cierre, y favorece a quienes mantienen su nivel durante toda la temporada. Es el terreno en el que Kane presume de regularidad y Yamal, de impacto en los grandes partidos.

articles.title: El boom de los coches retro: ¿negocio, moda o un arma contra los chinos?
articles.standfirst: La presentación del Citroën 2 CV consolida una tendencia en la industria del automóvil: la reedición de modelos míticos de las marcas europeas. Pero ¿qué hay detrás de esto?
articles.summary: La presentación del Citroën 2 CV consolida una tendencia en la industria del automóvil: la reedición de modelos míticos de las marcas europeas. Pero ¿qué hay detrás de esto?
articles.body: No es algo nuevo, aunque el Salón del Automóvil de París celebrado esta semana lo ha vuelto a poner de relieve: las marcas europeas apuestan por recuperar modelos icónicos de su pasado y actualizarlos con el diseño y la tecnología del siglo XXI para, además, convertirlos en eléctricos. Una receta de la que, por ejemplo, Fiat lleva varios años sacando rédito con su Fiat 500 y que, más recientemente, Renault ha imitado para sus eléctricos de nueva generación (Renault 5, Renault Twingo, Renault 8 Gordini incluso el Alpine A110). Ahora, la ofensiva viene de otro gigante de la automoción mundial: el grupo Stellantis. En París hemos visto el adelanto de la reedición del Citroën 2 CV, sin duda la estrella de la muestra, pero también un guiño al Fiat Multipla o la reedición del Peugeot 205 T16 como adelanto de lo que será el próximo 208. Pero… ¿cuáles son los motivos de esta fiebre por la nostalgia? Uno de los primeros argumentos que las marcas utilizaron para justificar estos revival de modelos clásicos que desaparecieron de sus gamas es el gancho para atraer a los conductores hacia lo eléctrico. En un principio todos pensamos que la tecnología eléctrica propiciaría nuevos códigos de diseño y proporciones respecto a los coches térmicos tradicionales y, de hecho, grandes fabricantes como Volkswagen incluso los diferenciaron por completo con nombres propios (la familia ID) y diseños completamente diferentes. Querían expresar claramente que eran ‘otra cosa’, pero el tiempo ha demostrado que ese planteamiento no fue acertado. Así que ahora el volantazo es total. Porque para atraer hacia lo eléctrico a los clientes más reacios se ha optado por revivir coches que fueron éxito en su tiempo, con un diseño moderno (eso sí), pero fuertemente inspirado en los clásicos. El Renault 5 E-Tech es el mejor ejemplo de este paradigma que, además, se ha visto acompañado de un éxito comercial, pero incluso Volkswagen ha ‘reculado’ en su estrategia, rebautizando sus eléctricos de nueva generación con nombres de su gama térmica actual (ID. Polo, ID. Tiguan) y acercándolos también a su diseño. De momento los alemanes no han reeditado modelos más … pero todo se andará. No menos importante para los fabricantes es el hecho de que parece que la fórmula funciona. El Fiat 500 así lo ha demostrado desde hace tiempo, como también ha sucedido con Mini, que ha construido una marca en base a la resurrección del ancestro británico. Más recientemente hay otros ejemplos, como especialmente el Renault 5 que, además, es el primer exponente de eléctrico low cost (aunque sólo en la versión más básica). Una buena razón para el éxito de esta fórmula es complementaria al ‘efecto llamada’ que pueda tener el diseño retro sobre el cliente. Y es que los fabricantes han aprovechado para adornar a la apelación a la nostalgia posicionando estos modelos en las gamas más bajas, aprovechando además que había un hueco en ese segmento de mercado, claramente por debajo de 30.000 euros. Así se ha construido la estrategia de Renault con el 5 (-25.000 euros) y el Twingo (-20.000 euros) y así lo va a hacer Citroën con el 2 CV, que será un rival de este último, pero sube la apuesta a los 15.000 euros. Y la tercera razón para la fiebre por lo retro no es menos importante. Se trata de una estrategia de ataque/defensa contra el coche chino ya que permite apelar a algo que las marcas orientales no tienen, ni podrán tener: historia. Las reediciones de modelos antiguos de éxito son una muestra de la trayectoria y el bagaje de los fabricantes europeos frente a los potentes argumentos de los coches asiáticos: el precio y la tecnología. De ahí que también se haya utilizado como justificación para esta estrategia. "Esa es la receta. Es la única manera de resistir frente a la competencia china. Ellos pueden copiarnos, pero no pueden quedarse con nuestro legado", explicaba Arnaud Belloni (CEO de Fiat y Lancia), ante la prensa en París. Eso sí, hay que jugar la baza con ciudado porque también se pone en juego ese legado: "Tu producto tiene que ser perfecto. Necesita tener un diseño perfecto, gran tecnología y tienes que ser leal al original. De lo contrario, lo estás traicionando".

articles.title: Greenard Ready To Explode As Eagles Edge Unit Faces Panthers
articles.summary: Jonathan Greenard is back healthy and hungry to prove his worth against Carolina. The Eagles' thin edge rush depth makes Sunday's matchup critical for the ve...
articles.body:
Jonathan Greenard is finally ready to play, and the Carolina Panthers better hope they are ready for him. The Eagles' starting edge rusher has been sidelined by injuries, but he is now cleared to face the Panthers on Sunday at Lincoln Financial Field. This is the moment Greenard has been waiting for since the season started. He has played in just two of Philadelphia's five games so far, but he is eager to show what he can do when he is fully healthy. The Panthers' offense will face a pass rusher who is desperate to get back on the field.

Greenard has not hidden his anger about missing time. He said the inability to play "hurts my soul and it eats me up." That kind of pain usually makes a player dangerous when they return. He is not just looking to be present; he wants to be effective. Greenard told reporters that he still feels like "one of the best at my position." He is confident he can beat anyone. The Eagles are 2-3 and on a three-game losing streak, so they need him to step up immediately. He knows the team needs a spark, and he plans to be that spark.

The veteran pass rusher described his ankle as the current focus while noting his pec is stronger. Fans and teammates mostly recognize him from his tenure with the Minnesota Vikings, he acknowledged. Now he gets a chance to rewrite that story. "It's a matter of me getting out there and actually showing it, putting it on tape," Greenard said, according to Sports Illustrated . He perceives light at the tunnel's end and stands prepared to reverse the situation. The Panthers cannot afford to give him a free pass on Sunday.

The Eagles do not have much depth at edge rusher right now. Greenard's return is vital because the unit is thin. He has been a late scratch for recent games, including the loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars in London. Now he is back, and the team needs him to hold the line. The Panthers have a tough road ahead. Greenard's presence changes the dynamic of the entire pass rush.

Greenard emphasized that availability constitutes the finest ability, yet he will participate only when effective. He wants to help the team win, not just take the field. Collaboration with the staff informs the decision, although he retains the ultimate authority. He joked that the team's injury list is "longer than a novel." Despite the adversity, he believes the team can use this pain as fuel. He is ready to prove that he belongs on the field with the best.

Philadelphia needs to stop their losing streak against a struggling Panthers team. The Eagles have missed their star quarterback Jalen Hurts for this game due to a blood clot in his calf. Tanner McKee will start in his place. The offense will have to work hard to score points while the defense tries to dominate. Greenard is the key to that defense. If he can get pressure on the quarterback, the Eagles have a chance to win. If he struggles, the thin edge unit could crumble under the pressure.

Greenard knows he has something to prove. He is not just playing for himself; he is playing for the team. The Panthers must prepare for a furious return from a player who has been frustrated for weeks. As Greenard said, "We gonna turn this s#$% around." The time for talk is over. It is time to play ball. The Panthers will need their best effort to survive the storm coming from the Eagles' edge rush.

articles.title: Jaguars look to match best six-game start in team history
articles.summary: As the Jaguars prepare to play their second straight game in London, they have an opportunity to do something they haven't done in 27 years — start the year...
articles.body:
As the Jaguars prepare to play their second straight game in London, they have an opportunity to do something they haven't done in 27 years — start the year 5-1.

The Jaguars last started 5-1 in 1999. That year, they finished 14-2 and lost in the AFC Championship, to the Titans.

This year, Jacksonville has a chance (thanks to the division it's in) to win enough games to secure the No. 1 seed. The next test is a big one, however.

The Texans have done well against the Jaguars in recent years. Quarterback Trevor Lawrence has a 3-7 record against the Texans, with eight touchdown passes and 11 interceptions in those games. Via NBC Sports research, no player since Lawrence's rookie season has thrown more interceptions against a single opponent than Lawrence against the Texans.

The Texans, meanwhile, have a 15-5 record in division games since DeMeco Ryans became the head coach. In those games, quarterback C.J. Stroud has a record of 12-5, with 24 touchdown passes and five interceptions.

articles.title: The 24 HOUR RULE: An Oregon Road Trip Package With Some Football
articles.summary: Travel plus football is a wonderful thing about adding Washington & Oregon to the B1G. Stillwater, this area ain’t.
articles.body:
Fine, this is Mt. St. Helen's and it's in Washington, not Oregon, but when I'm headed to the Pacific Northwest, the two states are basically interchangeable in their beauty.

My first jaunt to the area since the age of 3 or 4 came in April of 2025 when I travelled to Seattle to cover a Huskers softball 3-game set against a scrappy Washington Huskies squad (the Huskers took 2 of 3 in front of a crowd that ranks as one of the loudest I've encountered live so far, Michigan being the other).

It was also an excuse to spend around 10 days on the road around after the series' completion checking out trails and mountains and such armed with an annual National Parks pass I acquired at Badlands in South Dakota figuring it was a nice nod to the old man, a career NPS public servant who had passed away weeks before that journey.

This trip is shorter mainly due to waiting for my cross-country cruiser to get out of the body shop, but I'll head north on Sunday for a little fooling around (Huskers softball makes a trip to Eugene in July; I'll be rolling again.) before making my way back to Omaha.

This trip has had its fun, though. I stayed in Ogden, Utah on night one, which is just up I-15 from Brigham City where I lived for a few years when Dad worked at the Golden Spike National Historic Site. I then headed through southeast Oregon towards Eugene and much of that part of the state is sort of a Badlands of its own with rocky dusty peaks and scrub, almost desert-like in places. But the final approach is all forested mountains, lakes and winding roads – fun driving if you enjoy that sort of thing and I do.

Due to the fact that Eugene itself is devoid of cheap hotels with ratings, I drove by it and headed south where I had made a reservation at the Rice Hill Inn with a rating of 8.0 mainly due to clean rooms and super-friendly staff, both of which proved very accurate. Beyond that, I require only free coffee, a table at which to write, functional WiFi and the means to charge everything. Done and done.

And quite frankly, it would be hard to find a place which beat this truckers' exit for personality. Along with a couple other gas station/large mini-marts, there was a Flying J with a Subway and Cinnabon, not to mention some pretty decent wings and check-out agents who offered discounts on sodas, waters and the like for the purchase of…basically anything I was in the process of purchasing.

Nearby are other attractions such as an adult shop called Adult Shop. The truck parking has seemed often filled there. Across the street from the massive Flying J complex is a large fenced field, the place appearing to be a ranch for donkeys and mini-bison. The area is capped off by the K&R Drive Inn which looks straight out of Back to the Future or Friday Night Lights. The burger was average and the onion rings more powerful than medical-grade laxatives. But the milkshakes and ice cream, my gawd. The pineapple shake complete with chunks of real pineapple made the after-effects of the rings totally worth it. I filled up on all after a 10k jaunt on the forested banks of the Cooper Creek Reservoir, and, damn, doesn't it sound like time for some pictures?

But enough of my travelogue even if there may be a few more pics in the coming days. I'm hoping to spend a couple of them around Mt. Rainier where, on the previous trip, I managed to pick a day when everything above 7000 feet or so was fully socked-in with visibility of maybe a couple hundred yards in the thick fog. I still would like to see the peak even if trying to hike the summit is not in the cards this time around.

Also, the hotel by the park is wonderful place with little decked-out trailers available as rooms. Of course, I'm staying there. Crap, better make those reservations sometime today.

No Dylan isn't starting at QB, but don't be too sure you won't see him. Brock Thomas, the 3rd, now 2nd, stringer is a walk-on and a local boy. If the Blackshirts get on him, I'm guessing his rope isn't too long.

This will be a couple of teams playing with some urgency. Or desperation.

The Huskers (and their fans) are plenty pissed about the near-miss against Indiana, expecially given how much of it was self-inflicted as has so often happened in recent years. A second straight week of THAT would not improve the mood.

Oregon is basically playing a CFP elimination game as they already have two losses – as is every game forward since they will need get their shit together and win out to make their 3rd straight.

If you listen to the Joel Klatt podcast, you heard plenty of nice things from him both before the game and after. He was impressed by the fans in both their energy and their intelligence as a group, especially knowing when to shut up when the Huskers have the ball.

He also seemed a little flabbergasted the Huskers weren't in the Top 25 after taking the #5 Hoosiers the distance.

Jamir Conn and Rex Guthrie are both Out tonight. And Riley van Poppel popped up as again Doubtful on the availability list. The final one will be released 2 hours before gametime.

Conn especially is a rough loss after being injured in the Indiana game – can't help but wonder if Nick Marsh is getting behind everyone on the 75-yard TD pass and if a time-out still isn't called if Jamir is in there. Fine, I'm moving on.

The spread is Oregon -6 1/2 and yes, they're floundering a little. But talent level (if currently not playing up to it), Autzen Stadium's crowd, and the Huskers penchant for self-destruction likely all play into things.

I do believe in this 2026 roster more than any other in recent memory. And I'm also fully in show-cause mode in their ability to win a game against a top opponent. Both can be true. If any Husker team can break through though, it is this one.

articles.title: Lessons in Vanderbilt Football: Ole Miss
articles.summary: There were a lot of painful lessons in this one…
articles.body:
Last week's game was brutal. Ole Miss was in firm control throughout the first half then disaster struck at halftime to turn it from a dominant win into a downright ass kicking. Vanderbilt was being beaten by a Top 10 Ole Miss team coming off a big loss then a bye week, so it was somewhat expected they would come out hot and firing. The embarrassing and infuriating part was how Vanderbilt was doing mind-numbingly stupid things to make their lives so much easier. Before I give away everything, let's get to it…

Discipline is killing this team. Penalties happen. A linebacker is going to get a hand high and accidentlly snag a facemask. A DB or OL will slip and have to hold to avoid a big play against. False starts, other procedural penalties, and after-the-play personal fouls cannot happen. Vanderbilt had 3 false starts, 1 illegal shift (2 nd player went in motion before 1 st was fully set), and 2 personal fouls. Clinton Azubuike got involved in a scuffle between a DB, who should also have been penalized, and a Vanderbilt WR late and was flagged. That turned 2 nd and goal at the 2 into 2 nd and goal at the 17 that eventually was a FG. Jaylon Stone headbutted an offensive lineman after a 3 rd down stop and turned a FG attempt into a TD. That was an 8-point swing in the first 3 drives. It should have been 10-7 to end the first quarter, not 14-3.

Discipline goes beyond penalties, and the attention to detail is lacking in other ways. It was most obvious in the end-of-half sequence that gifted Ole Miss 14 points to turn a 28-3 lead into a 42-3 blowout. First, Jared Curtis did the most "I was playing at Nashville Christian this time last year" thing possible by scrambling around back at the Vanderbilt 5 with only 43 seconds left in the first half. He got loose with the ball and was hit hard enough to jar the ball out and send it bouncing towards the end zone for an Ole Miss TD on the recovery. Evan Hampton compounded the issue by attempting to return the ensuing kickoff and fumbling at the Vanderbilt 17. Ole Miss converted for another TD. Both mistakes were made by freshmen, but the coaches are responsible for making sure they are aware of the situation and know this is NOT the time to take risks.

Junior Sherrill deserves more respect as a WR1. He is not as explosive or terrifying on a play-by-play basis as some elite WRs, but he makes plays when called upon. He had his worst game of the year with "just" 5 catches for 55 yards. Still, that accounted for 16% of Vanderbilt's total offense. He did get some help from another WR in this game.

The OL has to sort some issues out. Beyond the penalties, it is so disjointed. They are struggling to identify and pick up blitzes and stunts. I do wonder if some of that is coming from the QB's inexperience. They are doing a piss poor job in run blocking, too. Averaging 2.8 yards per carry against a defense that, even after that performance, is averaging 4.3 yards per carry against. Between penalties and not consistently moving the ball on the ground, they are making their own lives miserable by getting into 3 rd and longs.Lyndon Cooper is obviously playing injured and is often in and out of the game. Gunner Givens is out today, too, and has been one of the worst culprits on penalties, so it will be interesting to see if his replacement can stake a claim to the job.

On special teams, the kicking specialists had a good evening, but the kick returners had issues. Brock Taylor made a 45-yard FG. Tyle Ebel also unleashed the rocket leg. His punts went 59, 48, 64, and 62 yards. The returns were 11, 13 (plus 5 for an illegal formation), 26 (negated to 13 by a hold), and a bounce-and-bobble fair catch. Averaging 58.3 yards per kick and netting 49.0 yards is how you flip field position. Hampton had the biggest return game gaff, but Dontae Carter also let a kickoff go over his head and bounce straight up at the 2. He had to field it and only returned the ball a few yards. Again, details. He has to make sure that ball is going into the end zone instead of being a bit lackadaisical.

Jared Curtis had a slightly below average game per QBR (47.2), but he got very little help. The freshman was 19 of 32 for 222 yards with 1 TD and 2 interceptions while being limited on the ground to just 2 yards from 6 attempts. Both interceptions went off both hands of his intended targets, so neither of them was on him. He was feeling pressure a bit early yet looked hesitant to tuck the ball down. His knee bruise may have influenced that. The tape should provide him with some learning experiences, and nothing was bad enough to think it was going to be a trend. Coming into the game, he was 2 nd in the SEC for air yards per pass attempt at 10.4. He is putting the ball downfield consistently and throws a very catchable, accurate deep ball. The intermediate timing routes are the biggest opportunity for improvement, but the OL needs to give him more chances for rhythm.

The pieces besides Sherrill in the passing game may be finding their niches. In a game where the offense really struggled, Ja'Cory Thomas had 3 catches for 60 yards, including a TD. At least two, if not all three, catches were 1v1 sideline throws. He is a problem for a lot of CBs at 6'3 and 215 pounds. Curtis has the ability to put dimes up for him to go get where even if Thomas does not have burner speed to separate, he has the height and vertical to win contested catches, just like the TD where the CB was flagged for DPI. Walter Taylor also had 2 catches for 40 yards with both coming on deep over routes where he got behind LBs and in front of safeties while crossing the field. He presents a big target at 6'7 and has good speed for that height. Cole Spence had a pair of catches for 27 yards, too, even with the drop-turned-interception. In all, 9 players were credited with a reception, and 8 of them caught a pass beyond the LOS. They may not find a great sidekick for Sherrill but having a host of players making small but important plays throughout the game would be nice, too.

Was any hope for the defense misplaced? Or maybe they were not as bad as the 52 points looks? They are really responsible for 38 points. You could maybe even argue about it being 34 since 1 TD drive was a a single play from 35 yards out. That is likely a FG anyway. Allowing 38 to Ole Miss is not … awful. It would be bang on their average (38.8), which was raised by the 52 points they scored against us. Being average on defense would be … fine. Arkansas's average for the season is 19.3.

Fold or refocus? After a significant loss that felt promising at Georgia, the team played one of their worst games and nuked almost every bit of optimism in the fan base. Clark Lea said they have implemented new in-practice penalties for procedural penalties. That is nice, but I am skeptical it fixes the overarching discipline issues. Today would be a good time to show some intelligence and focus.

Is the season sunk, or can a hog roast be a modicum of hope? Arkansas is bad. Bad enough for Vanderbilt to be favored by 5.5 points. That spread has crept down from earlier in the week, which is concerning. Vanderbilt needs to show improvement that can predict future success, not just eek out a win. This is by far the easiest opponent left. Florida has been scuffling but is playing Texas moderately close. Mississippi State is get walloped by LSU, but they have been dangerous plenty often and are without star QB Kamario Taylor. Taylor should be healed by the time the Commodores head to Starkville. Handling business today then heading to a Kentucky team that looks surprisingly strong before the bye week is a critical stretch for any bowl hopes.

articles.title: Kaylene Smikle scores, 3-point shooting struggles in Lady Vols basketball scrimmage
articles.summary: Lady Vols basketball won 109-79 in an open scrimmage Saturday. Maryland transfer Kaylene Smikle led the way with 30 points.
articles.body:
Lady Vols basketball held an open scrimmage Oct. 17, showcasing their completely new roster to fans for the first time at Food City Center.

Tennessee played four 10-minute quarters against the male practice players. The Lady Vols struggled in the first half, trialing by four points at the break. But the offense picked up the slack in the second half and won 109-79.

Forward Fatmata Janneh was in a walking boot. The Texas A&M transfer and one of Tennessee's top offseason additions tweaked the left ankle in practice the day before. The injury is not considered to be a long-term issue.

Maryland transfer Kaylene Smikle was as good as advertised in the scrimmage. The 6-foot guard scored 30 points, followed by Rylie Theuerkauf, a 5-9 guard, with 16 points. Tennessee shot 54.9% from the field (50-for-91) and 20% from 3-point range (6-of-30).

Kim Caldwell, Tennessee women's basketball coach in third season with Lady Vols

The Lady Vols are averaging 102 points per game in three scrimmages against male practice players as they prepare for an exhibition game against Florida A&M on Oct. 27 (6:30 p.m. ET, SEC Network+).

Here are takeaways from the the scrimmage.

Coach Kim Caldwell's lineups remain ever-changing.

Tennessee started Smikle, Theuerkauf, 6-2 forward Zhen Craft, 5-7 guard Jada Eads and 5-9 guard Naomi White. It wasn't long before Caldwell went to the bench for a new look, though.

Harrisoum Coulibaly, Aaliyah Moore and Kennedy Fauntleroy were the first players to enter the game off the bench. Every available player was used in scrimmage, while Smikle earned a heavy usage rate.

Which players look ready to make an impact?

Tennessee didn't have a shortage of offensive contributors. Twelve of the 13 active players logged at least one point. Shaelyn Steele was the only player to not score and she did not take a shot.

Smikle looks to be the player the offense will run through. The 6-foot forward had no issues getting to the basket, and made her presence felt on the inside. She finished 14-for-21 from the field. Smikle's outside game did struggle, though, making just one of her five 3-point attempts.

Theuerkauf struggled early, but looked better late in the second half. She had 16 points on 7-for-12 shooting. The Georgia transfer poured in 10 fourth-quarter points.

Freshman Gabby Minus had a strong second-quarter stretch with help from the half-court trap. The Lady Vols forced turnovers on back-to-back possessions, leading to easy fastbreak points for Minus, who finished with 6 points.

As much offense as Tennessee had, it did so with easy looks at the rim. Life wasn't as easy beyond the perimeter.

The Lady Vols made just six of their 30 attempts from 3-point range. White, the Northern Arizona transfer, who is expected to be one of the top shooting threats in the country, went 2-for-8 and all of her attempts were 3-pointers.

Minus, Eads, Fauntleroy, and Riley Makalusky combined to shoot 0-for-11 from the behind the arc. Harper Peterson was the only one to have success, making both of her 3-point attempts.

Tennessee also found itself in an early hole. The Lady Vols' defense faltered in the opening minutes, finding themselves in a 19-9 hole halfway through the first quarter. After facing the double-digit deficit, the Lady Vols did not allow another point for nearly four minutes.

The Lady Vols started the second quarter on an 8-0 run, but the scout team continued to hang around. The practice players carried a 48-44 lead into halftime.

Tennessee also struggled at the free-throw line. The team made three of its eight attempts. The Lady Vols didn't attempt a free throw until 5:06 remained in the second quarter.

articles.title: Chicago Bears activate Kyler Gordon, Dayo Odeyingbo to injured reserve
articles.summary: The Chicago Bears get some help in the secondary, but they lose one of their defensive linemen. @wiltfongjr has all the latest here.
articles.body:
The Chicago Bears announced several roster moves today, including activating defensive back Kyler Gordon from the Physically Unable to Perform list. Gordon has not played this season while rehabbing a calf injury he suffered in the offseason. He was in the midst of his 21-day practice window and was a full participant for all 9 practices over the last three weeks.

At yesterday's press conference, head coach Ben Johnson said this about Gordon, "He's done a great job taking everything that we've assigned him so far. I feel good about him — whether that's this week or next week — being able to contribute to this team and help us out, and there's a number of ways he can do that. But I'm encouraged with what I've seen so far."

On Thursday, defensive coordinator Dennis Allen met the media and said this about Gordon, "He's been working extremely hard. He's been great around the building. He's been doing everything we've asked him to do. I've been impressed with him."

It'll be interesting to see how the Bears deploy Gordon on Sunday against the Atlanta Falcons, because while most of his NFL experience has been at nickel, he's also played and practiced at corner and safety. His versatility, if he can stay healthy, will provide the Bears' defense a huge boost.

The Bears also signed defensive back Nick McCloud to the 53-man roster from their practice squad, placed defensive lineman Dayo Odeyingbo (quad) on injured reserve, and released safety Xavier Woods.

Odeyingbo is second on the team with 3 sacks, third with 3 tackles for loss, and he leads Chicago defensive linemen with 2 batted passes. He'll miss at least 4 games on IR.

Chicago also announced that they're elevating linebacker Buddy Johnson and running back Zavier Scott from the practice squad for Sunday's game. They'll revert to the practice squad after the game.

articles.title: Chiefs Must Trade For George Pickens To Fix Their Deep Threat
articles.summary: The Chiefs need a true deep threat to win another Super Bowl. George Pickens is the target, not just a cheap rental, according to Yahoo Sports.
articles.body:
The Kansas City Chiefs are 4-0 and humming along, but their passing game has a glaring hole that won't fix itself. Patrick Mahomes needs a receiver who can stretch the field and win contested catches, and Rashee Rice is out with a hamstring injury for Sunday's game against the Chargers. According to Yahoo Sports , general manager Brett Veach must target George Pickens before the November 10 trade deadline to give this team its best shot at a fifth ring. The team cannot rely on Xavier Worthy alone to do the heavy lifting downfield.

Pickens is the only name on the list who fits the bill for a true difference-maker. Following the failure to secure a long-term extension with the franchise tag in Dallas, his future past the 2026 season remains uncertain as he plays under that designation now. Should the Cowboys drop from contention, trading him may become their sole method to regain draft assets instead of watching him depart in free agency, presenting a difficult decision. While Jerry Jones would probably insist on a significant return, Kansas City might deem the expense justified if they view Pickens as Mahomes' primary target for the upcoming four or five years.

Some analysts suggest Darnell Mooney makes sense because he is cheap and fits the intermediate zone, but that is a short-term fix for a long-term problem. According to Arrowhead Addict , Mooney is averaging just 3.4 targets and 1.6 catches per game while playing third fiddle to Malik Nabers. He is a rental for a 2027 or 2028 seventh-round pick, which is not sexy and does not solve the lack of a dynamic playmaker. The Chiefs require a player who can alter a game instantly with a single touch, much like Tyreek Hill did during his tenure with the franchise.

Jerry Jeudy is another option mentioned by Yahoo Sports, but he would be a different kind of addition who does not necessarily require a massive trade package. Although his route-running skills suit Andy Reid's offense, he currently occupies a diminished role with the Cleveland Browns. While he could maximize his strengths in space, he lacks the superstar potential that Pickens brings to the table. Improvement does not strictly require a superstar for Kansas City, yet these three prospects possess such potential and deserve Veach's attention as the deadline nears.

The front office has spent years building a roster that can contend, and adding another wide receiver should be the priority right now. Off-field troubles and injuries plague Rashee Rice during his contract year, casting doubt on his long-term status within Kansas City. Despite possessing speed, Xavier Worthy has not yet solidified his status among the NFL's top wide receivers, resulting in a lack of a dependable WR3 for the squad. To execute a major move, George Pickens must lead the Chiefs' list, providing Kansas City with a true difference-maker.

Head coach Andy Reid stated that Rashee Rice and offensive tackle Josh Simmons will both sit out Sunday's matchup versus the Los Angeles Chargers. A right hamstring injury from Kansas City's Week 4 win over the Las Vegas Raiders hinders Rice, whereas Simmons deals with a back injury. With these key players out, the need for a high-end receiver becomes even more urgent as the team prepares for the playoff push. The clock is ticking toward November 10, and Veach must act now to secure the talent needed for another run.

articles.title: The Real Reason Kane’s Record-Breaking Assist Changed History
articles.summary: Patrick Kane breaks the U.S.-born assist record with a helper on Connor Bedard's goal. Read how this historic moment unfolded in Chicago.
articles.body:
Patrick Kane etched his name into the history books on Thursday night at the United Center. He recorded his 895th career assist, a helper that put Connor Bedard past the Winnipeg Jets net. This single play moved Kane past Phil Housley for the most assists ever by a U.S.-born player in the NHL. The crowd roared as the American legend cemented a legacy that few thought he would still be adding to at this stage of his career.

The goal came during a power-play situation where the Blackhawks held a 5-on-3 advantage. Bedard fired the puck home to score his first goal of the 2026-27 season. It was also the first goal of his career while wearing the captain's "C." Tyler Bertuzzi also earned an assist on the play, marking his 200th career helper in the league.

Connor Bedard has been the face of the franchise since he was drafted. He finally broke his goalless streak for the season in a way that mattered most. According to Yahoo Sports , Kane was genuinely impressed with the shot Bedard unleashed. The connection between the veteran star and the young captain seems to be growing stronger every time they step on the ice together. Their chemistry on the top line is becoming a major weapon for the team.

Roman Kantserov, a rookie who plays on the same line, watched the moment unfold with awe. He told RG.org that the reception Kane received when he returned to Chicago was unforgettable. "There are legends here, and Kane is back," Kantserov said. He noted that the crowd's energy was so loud that television cameras just could not capture the full feeling of the room. For a young player like Kantserov, sharing the ice with Kane is a dream come true.

Surpassing Phil Housley is a massive milestone for American hockey. Housley was a dominant force, but Kane's consistency over nearly two decades is what allowed him to reach the top spot. This record highlights the growth of U.S. talent in a sport that has long been dominated by Canadian and European players. "He's got the same drive and passion, which I think is going to have a long-lasting effect on a lot of these players inside that dressing room," Olczyk said.

Olczyk added that Kane's influence on the franchise will last a long time, regardless of how many points he scores from here on. The young players in the locker room see what it takes to stay at the top level for so long. They see the work ethic required to set a record that stood for years.

The Blackhawks now have a captain who has scored his first goal and a legend who has set a new standard. The team faces a tough schedule ahead, but the momentum from this game could be a turning point. Roman Kantserov admitted that he had to prove himself after skipping the AHL to join the big club. Kane and Bedard immediately placed him on the first power-play unit, a move that worked at once, he observed.

But for one night in Chicago, the focus was on a number that will stand for a long time: 895.

articles.title: Kids Marathon gets first repeat winner in event history
articles.summary: An estimated 800 children participated in the third annual Kids Marathon event as part of the 49th annual Detroit Free Press Marathon
articles.body:
A year ago, Tyler Medrano redeemed himself in the second Kids Marathon after finishing as the runner-up in the inaugural event in 2024. This year, he aimed for a new accomplishment: winning it again.

Medrano outpaced a group of nearly 800 children between the ages of 6 and 13 to become the first-ever back-to-back winner of the event during the third annual Kids Marathon, presented by Priority Health on Saturday, Oct. 17, part of the 49th annual Detroit Free Press Marathon .

The accomplishment took some time to sink in for the 13 year-old.

"I can't really believe I won again," Medrano said, winded from the race. "It was pretty surreal to run and finish first again."

Children's Hospital of Michigan Family Fun Day

Medrano, who attends Clifford Smart Middle School in Commerce Township, credited his cross country coach for preparing him for the race.

His father Steve Medrano had nothing but praise for his son's accomplishment.

"I'm extremely proud of him. He works extremely hard. He runs almost everyday," said Steve Medrano, noting Tyler's participation in soccer and cross country at school. "He sets a goal and works as hard as he can to achieve it."

Little dashers and Kid's marathon participants

Participants in the Kids Marathon had to track and complete their first 25.2 miles before Saturday, then dash across the finish line for the final mile on race day.

Of the total runners in the event, half were students from five Detroit Public School Community District schools as part of a program that offered free registration and running shoes, in addition to transportation and Savvy Sliders as a post-race treat.

Golightly Education Center, John R. King and Davison Elementary-Middle School returned for a third year, while Mark Twain School for Scholars and Bates Academy participated for the second straight year. Academy of the Americas, Edmonson Montessori Elementary and Fisher Magnet Upper Academy all took part for the first time.

New shoes put Detroit kids on track for marathon weekend

Since the event's inception, participation from the DPSCD schools has grown by 60%. The inaugural year saw 250 students and increased to 300 last year. This year's event showcased 400 students from the district.

Ocean Lewis, a sixth grader at Bates Academy, took part for the first time this year. The 11-year-old said she enjoyed her time, but said it went by "super quickly."

Lewis, a cheerleader and swimmer, said she is proud to have run in the Kids Marathon.

"I feel like past [me] wouldn't expect me to do be doing this," she said.

Lewis' mother, Khadeejah Lasuc Lewis, credited the school district for introducing Lewis to the event.

"Running a marathon wasn't even anything we considered until she brought the flyer home from school and was excited to do it," Lewis said. "I love the 25 miles ahead because it's gotten her outside and running and tracking. So it's cool for her to be able to set a goal and plan for it and track, so I think there's a lot of benefits to that, too, outside the physical benefits."

When the Kids Marathon began two years ago, the mission indeed was to help the children learn how to set goals and build healthy habits. Davison Principal Randall Coleman has seen the change in his students.

"Our track and field team has definitely expanded with us participating in this program, and we want to get kids out from off the cell phones and in front of the video games to get them out active and healthy," Coleman said. "So this has been a great incentive for those students, and our numbers have increased every year that we've participated."

John Carson, dean of students and athletic director of John R. King, said this event is all about opportunity.

"What it really comes down to is having opportunities for kids to participate in something," Carson said. "Obviously, when you have things for them to do, they'll get engaged, and obviously parent participation is really key. So they're supporting the effort by letting the kids participate in events like this, and be a part of all these athletics and running."

articles.title: Which Oregon commits, 2028 recruits are on campus for game vs. Nebraska?
articles.summary: Oregon will welcome back top commits Rashad Streets and Tae Walden Jr., as well as several 2028 recruiting targets for Saturday's game vs. Nebraska.
articles.body:
The Oregon Ducks are welcoming back several talented recruits and commits once again this weekend against the Nebraska Cornhuskers . They will hope to give the incoming talent a better show than last week's loss to UCLA.

There are expected to be at least 15 recruits on the sideline for Saturday's game, with the potential for the list to expand. Among those visitors are seven committed players in the 2027 class, highlighted by five-star edge rusher Rashad Streets and four-star athlete Tae Walden Jr.

Streets makes the trip from Raleigh, North Carolina, and is one of Oregon's top commits. So far in his senior season, Streets has compiled 60 tackles, 33.5 tackles for loss, and 13 sacks in seven games at Millbrook High School. He is a top-30 recruit in the country, and he has remained steadfast in his commitment to the Ducks , even being one of the more vocal commits on social media, recruiting other players.

Walden was a splashy add to the class over the summer, as the Ducks pulled off the comeback win in the recruiting race after getting his final official visit. Walden is a star at wideout and corner, and he has the potential to play both sides in Eugene. However, Walden has stayed close with Ole Miss and was on campus for the Rebels' emotional win over LSU, so the Ducks have some competition to contend with.

So far this season, Walden has made 47 catches for 797 yards and nine touchdowns as a receiver, while making 16 tackles and six deflections defensively. This is the first time Walden will be on campus this fall, so the Ducks must do what they can to impress him and keep the Tennessee product roped in to Oregon's process.

Also in attendance, the Ducks will welcome four-star linebacker Toa Satele and four-star offensive lineman Gus Corsair , who is back in Eugene for a second consecutive game. In-state commits Malachi Garlington , George VanSandt and Josh Christensen will also return for another game day visit.

Satele, the No. 1 player from Hawaii in the 2027 class, is another guy who could make an immediate impact next season, and he isn't returning to Eugene alone. Satele's younger brother, Trison, is one of the top defensive linemen in the 2028 class and is already a priority target for the Ducks.

Oregon is also hosting 2028 wideout Jayce Halasz for the second weekend in a row and third game-day visit this season. The Washington recruit is heavily considering the Ducks, and he is returning for a second-straight game after not getting to spend enough time with the Ducks last week because of the early kickoff. He has 19 catches for 431 yards and seven touchdowns this season at Graham-Kapowskin High School.

Another intriguing wideout in the class will make his way to Eugene this weekend, as Quincey Clay, the top player in Idaho, will visit the Ducks for the first time. He saw Oregon in action in Los Angeles against USC, and he left Southern California with an offer from the Ducks. Now, he will visit with the potential to become another big Idaho recruiting win for Dan Lanning , following wins with Kenyon Sadiq and Gatlin Bair .

The Ducks are closely linked to 2028 quarterbacks Josiah Boyd and Tristin Gaines , but they are keeping their options open, hosting four-star quarterback Luke Rubley from Aurora, Colorado. A 6-foot-3 passer, Rubley has tossed 15 touchdowns against six interceptions this season, while completing 60.6% of his passes.

Oregon will also host four-star offensive lineman Grayson Williams and four-star defensive lineman Geraci Carson, both of whom are top-100 players in the 2028 class from the Southeast. Carson is a big target in an area the Ducks didn't recruit well in the 2027 class, but LSU and Ole Miss are currently top contenders for the Mississippi recruit. Also, 2029 offensive tackle Sonny Lefotu and his brother, 2028 linebacker Isaiah Lefotu, will both visit from Bakersfield.

Oregon and Nebraska are set to kick off on Saturday at 8 p.m. PT, with the game airing live on Fox.
